verification_report.summary:
The full proof passes sequential verification under the stated accepted inputs. All mixed products and sublevel integrals are well defined and finite for the fixed bounded potentials. Strict positivity of the Hermitian background supplies B_0 and the epsilon omega reserve; no closedness or uniform mass bound is used.

The mixed ordered-contact proof is valid with every remaining factor held fixed. Locality identifies the maximum's measure with the lower potential's measure on compact subsets of contact. Uniform convergence, the compact-set weak-limit inequality and inner regularity give the asserted restricted measure inequality. This requires no envelope contact theorem. The bounded Stokes identity follows from the accepted smooth decreasing exact-background regularization: the approximating differences are uniformly bounded and converge in capacity, so the accepted continuity with quasi-continuous coefficients passes every torsion term to the limit.

For p=n-k-1, the five derivative coefficients are exactly k, p, k(k-1), 2kp and p(p-1), with the displayed signs and powers. Replacing the two or three background factors by the positivity reserve gives indices k-1, k, k-2, k-1 and k, respectively. Grouping after epsilon^(-2)<=epsilon^(-3) yields k(k-1), k(1+2p) and p^2. Each is at most n^2. Consequently a=B_0 n^2 s epsilon^(-3)<1/32, q=1-4a>7/8, and 1+q^(-1)+q^(-2)<4 establish the induction, including zero integrals and absent indices. Thus q^n I_0<=I_n and q^(-n) tends to one. In dimension one ddc W=0; in dimension two only the single ddc omega terms survive. In dimension three the grouped coefficient triples are (0,0,4), (0,3,1), (2,2,0). All small-dimensional cases are valid.

The positive-volume lemma correctly uses upper semicontinuity of the first qpsh function and the canonical representative of the second. A local submean inequality with a smooth correction turns an almost-everywhere upper bound into the required pointwise bound. No upper semicontinuity of a difference is assumed.

For every fixed c<1, the epsilon and s choices are compatible, and the infimum makes each selected sublevel set nonempty without requiring attainment. Writing M=integral_U omega_v^n and V=integral_U omega^n, strict domination produces [q^n(1-epsilon)^n-c]M+q^n epsilon^n V<=0 with M>=0 and V>0, an immediate contradiction even if M=0. Individual nonzero mass follows using the constant sup_X u+1. Exponential comparison follows with the unchanged current of v-t and c=exp(-lambda t), then t decreasing to zero.

The attribution to [GL22, Theorem 1.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2106.04272) is verified against the supplied text and primary PDF. Its printed (n-1)^2 and larger intermediate coefficient are not substituted for the manuscript's independently checked n^2 and exact coefficient. [KN15, Theorem 0.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5491) is also verified; its different ddc normalization and torsion constant are not identified with the present ones. No modified comparison, domination, weak exponential comparison, BMP, PVP, density assumption or envelope contact-support result is imported.
